summary: Phase 2 per-app CD workflows pass Review C at audited HEAD 1902a8215 on the re-review after remediation. Green commit 3f1c33b9a added a tag-lookup block to each of the six sections of docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md and a dated note to docs/runbooks/storytime-deploy.md. Green commit bbe334bff passes the pushed commit to the marketing build and records the sales push as an open limit. Every gcloud command form of the runbook ran live as a read-only call and returned the expected shape. The service, region, and project names match scripts/ci/apps.json and each cloudbuild file. The sales input sources match the scripts the runbook names. The Open limits text matches the code. The select step still logs the affected ids, and the job names still name each app. One Nit remains: the gcloud builds list fallback says 'read the newest build id' in projects that hold builds of several apps.
contract_applicability: applicable: the phase changes operator-facing contracts (two CD workflows, the select-step CLI consumption, the matrix substitutions wiring, the app table, the tag rule, and two runbooks). No browser UI exists, so no browser inspection ran; the dedicated UX browser auditor is not duplicated, and no durable Playwright testing started.
nonblocking_findings: C31 [Nit] docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md: The gcloud builds list fallback of the primary-advantage, accounts, and marketing sections says 'read the newest build id'. The primary-advantage project holds the builds of two apps, and the reading-advantage project holds the builds of five. A manual traffic build can also be the newest build. The fallback can name a build of another app or a traffic build, and the derived tag then fails the tag-exists check of the same block. Rationale: The primary path of each section (the GitHub Actions job log of the push job) names the push build exactly, so the documented operator flow works end to end and the phase contract holds. The fallback alone can mislead on the first read at a human-gated step. One line that says how to pick the build (match the createTime with the push, or read the id only in the GitHub job log) closes it. Owner: Green.
evidence: Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD returned 7721962d2a76923715aff3fba85f5402b08207db, past the audited HEAD 1902a8215. The two newer commits belong to storytime_at_home_release_20261106 and touch no phase path (git diff --stat 1902a8215..HEAD over .github, scripts/ci, docs/runbooks, 'apps/*/cloudbuild*.yaml', and measure/tracks/per_app_cicd_20261107 prints nothing, exit 0). git status --porcelain over the phase files prints nothing, so the working tree equals 1902a8215 for every audited file. The remediation commits 3f1c33b9a and bbe334bff sit in the ancestry of 1902a8215 (git log d28f8fd52..1902a8215 lists them), and 8380479ea is the Red test commit of the r4 round.

B1 withdrawn: each of the six sections of docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md now holds a find-the-tag block. primary-advantage, accounts, and marketing name _TAG from the build id of the push (pa- and ac- plus the first 8 characters, c plus the first segment of the UUID-checked BUILD_ID), sales-advantage names _PUSH_BUILD_ID, and accounting and codecamp-advantage state the fixed tags candidate and sso-candidate with the tag-holder describe commands and the newest-revision comparison. The service, region, and project names match scripts/ci/apps.json and the deploy steps of the push files: primary-advantage-app in primary-advantage; accounts, accounting, codecamp-advantage, marketing, and sales-advantage in reading-advantage; all in asia-southeast1. The tag derivations match the push files: primary, accounts, and storytime hold env BUILD_ID with --tag=<prefix>-$${BUILD_ID:0:8}; marketing holds the UUID check and candidate_tag c$${build_id%%-*}; accounting holds --tag=candidate in both branches; codecamp holds --tag=sso-candidate; sales holds --tag=legacy-rollback and --tag=candidate. The general rule names the GitHub Actions run 'CD - gated apps', the job 'Build <app> with no traffic', and the step 'Submit Cloud Build', which match the workflow names and print the Cloud Build id. W-22 of cd-workflows.test.mjs pins the six sections and their variables. This review proved every command form live (see the commands list).

N2 withdrawn: the sales section block 'Where the other substitutions come from' matches the code. apps/sales-advantage/scripts/verify-sales-release-inputs.mjs requires the exact lowercase 40-character commit (validateReleaseInputs), reads the backup run with the Cloud SQL Admin API (sqladmin.googleapis.com projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/backupRuns/<id>), requires status SUCCESSFUL, type ON_DEMAND, the description sales-curriculum-before-<commit>-not-before-<boundary>, and an endTime after the boundary, and rejects a boundary in the future or older than 1 hour (ONE_HOUR_NANOSECONDS). apps/sales-advantage/scripts/create-sales-release-archive.sh validates the 40-character form, resolves the commit with git rev-parse --verify, and archives exactly that commit with git archive. The traffic file step verify-curriculum-backup calls the script with $_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA, $_CURRICULUM_BACKUP_NOT_BEFORE, the project, the instance cloud-sql, and $_CURRICULUM_BACKUP_ID; no step creates a backup. W-26 pins the three input names in the sales section.

N1 withdrawn: docs/runbooks/storytime-deploy.md holds the dated Note (2026-11-07) directly under the '## Steps' heading, before numbered steps 1 and 2. It says a push that affects storytime builds the revision with --no-traffic and the tag st-<first 8 characters of BUILD_ID>, that steps 1 and 2 apply only when the workflow did not run for the commit, and that the traffic move (step 4) still waits for Daniel's word. cd-apps.yml builds every affected gated row under the job name 'Build ${{ matrix.id }} with no traffic' with no traffic step (git grep for cloudbuild-traffic, update-traffic, and --to-latest in .github/workflows at 1902a8215 exits 1). apps/storytime/cloudbuild.yaml deploys with --no-traffic and --tag=st-$${BUILD_ID:0:8} and holds no update-traffic step. The storytime row of scripts/ci/apps.json is gated with project primary-advantage and service storytime-app.

N3 withdrawn: the evidence-class limit is still true and is now recorded. No Cloud Build run has run an edited push or traffic file (the newest reading-advantage build lists as 2026-09-24), and the Open limits section states 'No traffic file has run. The files are checked as text only.' Phase 4 tasks 4.1, 4.2, and 4.5 keep the live proofs as the gate. The owner of N3 was none, and the runbook now records the limit.

Open limits text versus code (commit bbe334bff): apps/marketing/cloudbuild.yaml declares exactly one REQUIRED_ default, _RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA, so the select-step substitutions() of cd-apps.yml returns --substitutions=_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA=<HEAD_SHA> for the marketing row, and the build job consumes ${{ matrix.substitutions }} in the gcloud builds submit command. HEAD_SHA binds github.sha, the pushed commit, and the validate-release-input step of the marketing push file accepts it as the 40-hex form. apps/sales-advantage/cloudbuild.yaml declares three REQUIRED_ defaults (_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA, _CURRICULUM_BACKUP_NOT_BEFORE, _RELEASE_SOURCE_MANIFEST_SHA256), so the field stays empty and the job passes no substitution; the first step validate-release-inputs runs release-source-manifest.mjs verify and verify-sales-release-inputs.mjs inputs, which refuse the defaults, so the sales push build fails there. The regex ^  (_[A-Z0-9_]+): "REQUIRED_" of the select step matches the substitution blocks of both files exactly. W-24, W-25, and W-26 of cd-workflows.test.mjs pin this behavior, and the Open limits bullet of traffic-moves.md states it as the code behaves.

Matrix substitutions and operator-visible output: the matrix rows of cd-apps.yml carry the new field substitutions, computed from the push file of each affected gated row (empty for a missing file, which fails the submit closed). Both workflows' select steps log 'echo "affected: $ids"' exactly once (git grep -c), which names each affected app. The job names 'Select affected apps', 'Build ${{ matrix.id }} with no traffic', and 'Deploy to Cloud Run' name each app in the GitHub UI. The two select steps are text-equal after the r4 change (W-18c), and the www deploy job consumes only the www output, so the copied matrix code stays unused there and harmless.

Live read-only proof (2026-11-08, this review, no secret printed): gcloud run revisions list for accounts returned accounts-00011-vs8. The runbook describe forms returned: accounts tag list empty (no push has run the new tag rule, so the check fails closed as designed), accounting filter tag='candidate' revision accounting-00007-tuz, codecamp-advantage filter tag='sso-candidate' empty (no candidate revision exists yet), marketing tag list c008d2296,cb0d04cbd,c2a619e22,c027a7d9b,c08fd00a1,cbd883d25,c032b2903,c30d2bbc0 (each c plus 8 hex characters, the runbook tag shape), sales-advantage filter tag='candidate' revision sales-advantage-00019-zir, and primary-advantage-app tag list rehearsal1,rehearsal2,cutover,rehearsal3,cutover2,deploy4,deploy3,deploy5,approved,a35 (no pa- tag yet, expected). gcloud builds list for reading-advantage printed UUID build ids, which proves both tag derivations (the first 8 characters and the first segment are the same 8 characters). gcloud run revisions list for storytime-app returned storytime-app-00011-dut as the newest revision, which matches the live-revision fact of docs/runbooks/storytime-deploy.md.

Test evidence relied on: Review A at the same pinned HEAD re-ran the targeted suite through heavy-run (EXIT=0, 119 passed: 107 scripts/ci tests plus 12 storytime guard tests) and the sales guard line (28 passed, 1 known approval failure). This review ran no test suite; it re-verified every operator contract by reading the files at 1902a8215 and by the live read-only gcloud calls above.

Re-review scope: no CONTEST item was routed to this review, so no dispositions line is required. The earlier findings B1, N1, N2, and N3 of review-c-09ce375d2.json were fixed by Green commits 3f1c33b9a (the two runbooks) and bbe334bff (the two workflows and the Open limits bullet); this review withdraws each of them above. The new finding C31 is a Nit and routes to Green.
